spine.active_goal: Retire the v1 file ledger by freezing it as a grep-only archive and stand v2 up fresh. ALL FIVE CRITERIA NOW MET: archive frozen and byte-verified, 7 threads seeded, skills renamed/published, and criterion 5 closed 2026-07-26 - core.hooksPath reconciled and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA resolving both PROVEN, live /lift-off and /ledgerize both demonstrated. Eligible to close; the outstanding guard work is NOT in its criteria and belongs to a successor thread.
spine.next_step: DECIDE FIRST: all 5 criteria met, so close this thread and open a successor for the guard work. Guard task: invert the rule at hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:76 to deny-by-default - any resolvable token under a protected root DENIES unless the head is on a read-only allowlist. Keep shell-tokens.mjs as-is. Prove both ways: the 12 verified evasions flip to DENY, the 41-command read-only corpus stays ALLOW. Then suite, re-review, merge, publish, re-install. DO NOT merge before that - see 0011.
open_risks: BLOCKED: fix/pre-tool-use-guard must NOT merge. 20 commands the old guard DENIED are ALLOWED by it; 12/12 reproduced independently. `( rm -rf <root> )` and `sudo rm -rf <root>` both pass. See decision 0011.

Root cause is architectural: pre-tool-use.mjs is allow-unless-provably-destructive over a hand-rolled bash parser. Every parse gap is a silent evasion. Fix is to invert to deny-by-default within the root, not to enumerate gaps.
The STATUS QUO IS SAFER. Live install is 0fe1c02, which over-blocks reads but resists evasion. There is no urgency to ship the branch. Shipping it as-is would net-weaken protection of the store.

REFUTED (was the top risk): CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA IS delivered to hooks and the real store IS protected today. ledger-roots.mjs is byte-identical across 0fe1c02 and b0e1079. The old probe measured the env-absent fallback. See 0007.

Uncovered by BOTH guards, out of scope for the guard branch: ref-level destruction (git update-ref -d refs/heads/_ledger, git branch -D _ledger) and deletion of <repo>/.git/worktrees/ledger-worktree. The ref is the authoritative data.
scanSegments is quadratic in tokens per segment (128k tokens = 15.2s) against a 10s hook timeout, so the guard fails OPEN under a large single-line command. Any size cap added must fail CLOSED.

The v2 store is git-ref-backed at refs/heads/_ledger, not a working directory. Read thread state with `git show refs/heads/_ledger:threads/<id>.json`. An ls of <repo>/.git/ledger shows an empty dir and looks like data loss - it is not.

Concurrent sessions write ONE store: this session's decisions landed as 0007, 0008, then 0011, so another session took 0009/0010 mid-work. Never assume decision numbers are contiguous or that you hold the latest state.

COMPLETION CRITERIA ARE IMMUTABLE after open_thread - update_thread only toggles done on existing text and rejects the whole call on unknown text. Get criteria right at creation; later work lands in the spine.

Live tool names are mcp__plugin_session-continuity_ledger__*. Never re-use the old mcp__ledger__* ToolSearch check to test whether the server is loaded - it false-negatives even when the server IS running.
Spine list items are capped at 300 chars each; an over-cap item rejects the WHOLE update_thread call rather than truncating.
`chmod -R a-w` is an accident guardrail, not tamper resistance. Never call the freeze immutable. `.git/info/exclude` is clone-local; a fresh clone is protected only by .claude/.gitignore:42.
Three v1 threads were deliberately NOT carried into v2 (decision 0002). Their open items exist ONLY in the frozen archive and nothing will surface them at resume.
